newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic, Nynex deny report of 10,000 job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic, Nynex deny report of 10,000 job cuts.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp. and Nynex Corp. Tuesday denied a published report that they planned to cut 10,000 jobs or more after completing their merger.

The companies said they planned to cut 3,000 management positions within three years, as previously announced. The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the plan, reported Tuesday that the companies were likely to cut 10,000 jobs within five years after the merger.

The newspaper's sources said there was no hard number of cuts established, but that depending how quickly the companies can consolidate back-room operations, as many as 15,000 jobs might eventually be eliminated.

Bell Atlantic and Nynex said they had no plans for any cuts other than the 3,000 already announced. The companies said they will respond to competition by cutting costs and improving efficiency, and that some parts of Bell Atlantic's business were adding employees to meet new opportunities.
The companies have received Justice Department approval for their merger, but still await a ruling from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.

The companies have a combined total of 137,000 employees. The Journal story said the original estimate of 3,000 cuts was deliberately conservative to avoid arousing criticism such as AT&T Corp. received when it announced plans to cut 40,000 jobs.
